title: Carrier jet
world: A seventies navy fighter on a carrier's deck at dawn. It lives in salt spray, jet blast and hydraulic fluid, launched and caught again and again, tended between launches by a deck crew in coloured jerseys. Everything on it was put there by someone with a job to do: masked, stencilled, touched up, worn in. A government machine that its squadron wears with pride.
feel: A squadron's pride on a working machine

colours.name: Deck jerseys
colours.say: the crew's own colours: yellow, green, purple, brown, blue

materials.name: Semi-gloss gull grey, chalky where the sun hits

surfaces: How it ages: paint touched up in fresher patches, panel by panel; salt and hydraulic grime collecting low and behind the wheels and running back with the air; metal near the heat turned straw, blue and bronze; the places boots go scuffed dark.
language: How its marks behave: hard, masked edges; marks that follow the airframe's own lines and run where the air runs; small stencilled words that do a job; red where it's dangerous, black where the crew works, blue and gold where it's proud. Nothing decorative without a reason, except the squadron's colours, which are the reason.
identity: An invented squadron in blue and gold. Its emblem: a gold lightning bolt on a blue disc in a thin gold ring. Its colours can run big; its emblem can appear at any size. Its name is never written.
words: Small stencils are welcome where a jet would carry them (the user said yes to small words, 2026-10-07); no other lettering.
license: Inspiration, not a list: use any of this, or none of it, and invent the car's own pieces in this language. Compose the whole car first; let the large and medium things run across the pieces and end where the car's flow ends.
